trust_decision.summary: LocalCommandExecutor implementations trust the program, argument and environment strings: they concatenate them into one command line handed to bash -c / cmd /c with no escaping, so any value a caller can influence becomes shell syntax.

landing_point.why: The report only names LocalCommandExecutor; on the platform the tests run on, this is the one line that pastes each argument into a bash -c string, and it is the line the advisory's example (a contingency/DSL option containing shell syntax) reaches.

fix_sites.entry_point: LocalComputationManager.execute(...) on Windows -> WindowsLocalCommandExecutor.execute(...), program word from SimpleCommand.getProgram()/GroupCommand sub-commands

O3_reason_to_dismiss: A solver working on Linux can argue the Windows executor is a separate, untestable platform path and that environment names and the program word come from the application's own ExecutionEnvironment/SimpleCommand API rather than from a user-supplied case or DSL file, so only the reported argument shape needs quoting.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Environment names ending in PATH must keep the trailing self-reference (: $NAME on Unix, %NAME% on Windows) OUTSIDE the quotes so the child process still inherits the parent PATH; wrapping the whole NAME=VALUE word in quotes, or escaping the $ / % in that suffix, breaks resolution of the program (e.g. itools) that every distributed execution launches.

O6_input_shapes: single argument containing a double quote that closes the old "..." wrapper (Unix and Windows)
single argument containing a single quote that breaks out of the new '...' wrapper (Unix '\'' idiom)
newline / carriage return inside an argument or an environment value
$(...) or backtick command substitution inside an environment value (Unix)
%VAR% expansion inside an argument or an environment value (Windows)
trailing backslashes before the closing quote of an argument (Windows)
the environment variable NAME itself as the injected item (rejected on Windows, untouched on Unix)
the program name as the injected item (rejected on Windows, untouched on Unix)
a whole List of arguments plus a whole Map of environment entries, each element escaped individually rather than one plain string

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Unix implementation appends the environment variable NAME unquoted and unvalidated; a name such as X=$(touch /tmp/p) or X=1;touch /tmp/p is evaluated as an assignment word by bash, so the injection happens through the name, not the value
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: environment names come from the application's ExecutionEnvironment map and no caller in this repository supplies any, so the route is not attacker-reachable
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file as the landing point, 0 files

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Unix implementation appends the program name raw with no quoting or validation, while the Windows half of the same fix rejects quotes and spaces in the program name
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: the program word is a constant chosen by the caller (ITOOLS_PRG = "itools"), never read from a case or DSL file
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file as the landing point, 0 files

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Windows program word is unquoted at the pinned commit and the published fix only rejects '"' and space, leaving & | ^ < > % in the program word able to chain a second command inside cmd /c
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: developer-supplied program name, and the Windows path cannot be exercised on a Linux test runner
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: 1 file, same package as the landing point

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a third LocalCommandExecutor backend (ssh/slurm/k8s style) that builds a command line for a remote shell
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the repository already ships three LocalCommandExecutor implementations across two modules; adding a transport that shells out through ssh is the obvious next backend and it would copy the Unix quoting helper or forget it entirely

O8b_injection_room.sibling: another name-suffix rule appended to the unquoted assignment word (e.g. a second well-known variable that must stay self-referential)
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the PATH/:$NAME branch already special-cases one name and appends shell-expanded text deliberately, so a maintainer extending that branch would add another unescaped fragment next to the escaped value

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a shared quoteCommandLine hook in the abstract base with one subclass failing to apply it
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: both executors duplicate the same build-then-ProcessBuilder pattern, so the natural refactor is to lift quoting into the base class, which is exactly where a new implementation would silently skip it

O9_family: OS command injection (CWE-78) with argument-injection flavour (CWE-88): unsanitised shell command-line construction

O10_build.toolchain: Maven multi-module build (parent powsybl-parent v29, powsybl-core 7.4.0-SNAPSHOT)
O10_build.project_tests: computation-local/src/test/java/com/powsybl/computation/local/LocalCommandExecutorTest.java only checks that the no-timeout overload delegates; LocalComputationManagerTest.java drives fake executors. The fix adds LocalCommandExecutorSecurityTest with four tests, three of them @EnabledOnOs(OS.WINDOWS) so on a Linux runner only the Unix test runs. computation-local-test needs Docker (testcontainers) but the affected module executes only local bash/cmd.
